mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next 5 trading days, investors anticipate future rate hikes, causing a short-term discounting effect that depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp over the next 5 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified trigger window (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rise is ≤0.25pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) of at least 0.3% for two consecutive months reduces the real discount rate applied to equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified inflation decline, or decline is <0.3% per month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) by at least 10% over the next 5 days signals strong labor demand, prompting firms to raise capital expenditures and expand earnings guidance, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10% over the next 5 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the trigger, or PAYEMS increase is <10%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 2% followed by a rebound of ≥3% in the next month creates a 'double-bottom' pattern in supply chains, which reduces uncertainty and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60-day period.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls ≥2% in month T, then rises ≥3% in month T+1
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the recovery window, or the rebound is <3%.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) exceeds 10% above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months, it signals a sustained housing recovery that lowers financing costs and boosts corporate earnings expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥10% above 12-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the trigger, or the increase is not sustained for two months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) of at least 1% indicate excess liquidity accumulation, which lowers risk premia and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the liquidity decline, or decline is <1% per month.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls by more than 0.5 percentage points over the next 3 months, it signals a strengthening labor market, prompting optimism about wage growth and corporate profit margins, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.5pp over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the unemployment decline, or decline is ≤0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 (GDP) and INDPRO by at least 2% in the same quarter, followed by a rebound in GDPC1 of ≥3% in the next quarter, creates a supply-side recovery narrative that reduces recession risk and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 down ≥2% and INDPRO down ≥2% in quarter T, then GDPC1 up ≥3% in quarter T+1
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the recovery quarter, or the rebound in GDP is <3% or INDPRO does not decline.
